title: Mobile nail technology scope and skin and nail boundaries
audience: Mobile nail technicians who offer manicure, pedicure, gel and acrylic services at a client location
learningOutcomes: Decide whether a nail service is inside the approved scope for the business
Identify when a client's nail or skin condition means the service is declined and the client is referred
Explain why some councils classify artificial nail work as a higher-risk service

instruction.heading: Scope for mobile nail work
instruction.body: Mobile nail work in this course covers natural nail care, manicure and pedicure, and the application and removal of gel polish, dip powder and artificial nail products. Work on intact skin and nails is in scope. Work on infected, inflamed, broken or wounded skin or nails is not. The technician declines it and suggests the client see a health professional.

instruction.heading: Council and state position
instruction.body: Some councils place artificial nail services in a higher-risk category that needs registration or periodic renewal. Others classify nail work differently. The position depends on the location and the council, and the business records which applies for each service area. UNCONFIRMED: no official source has been fetched for this point in this draft. A reviewer must confirm it before approval.

instruction.heading: Declining and referring
instruction.body: The technician asks about medical conditions, recent infections, diabetes, circulation problems and any product reaction before starting. If the client has a condition that makes the service unsafe, or the nail or skin shows signs of infection, the technician does not carry out the service. The decline is recorded and the client is told why, in plain words, without giving a diagnosis.

procedure: Check the requested service against the approved service list for the business and the service area
Ask the health and product questions and record the answers before starting
Look at the nails and the skin around them, and decline if there are signs of infection, injury or inflammation
If the service is declined, explain the reason and suggest the client see a health professional
Record the service carried out, or the decline, on the booking

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a gel manicure. Her nail beds are red and swollen around one nail, and she has a recent infection.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Does the technician carry out the gel manicure?
workedExamples.reasoning: Signs of infection on the nail or surrounding skin are outside the service. The technician declines, records the reason, tells the client to see a health professional, and does not offer a workaround on the day.

equipmentAndPpe: Approved service list for the service area
Good light and a clean working surface
Gloves and single-use items for each client

commonErrors.error: Carrying out artificial nails on an infected or inflamed nail.
commonErrors.prevention: Decline the service, record it and refer the client.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the council rule applies everywhere.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the council position for each service area before offering the service.
Say what was observed and suggest a health professional. Do not name a condition.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Some councils classify artificial nail services as higher-risk and require registration. This lesson does not say which council applies. UNCONFIRMED: no official source has been fetched for this point in this draft. A reviewer must confirm it before approval.
Completing this lesson does not give registration, a licence or authority to carry out any regulated service.

qualityStandard: Every service is on the approved list for the service area
Health intake is completed before any service
Each declined service is recorded with the reason
documentationEvidence: Approved service list with council position and review date
Record of each service or decline
summary: Mobile nail work covers intact nails and skin only
Council and state positions differ, so the service area is checked
Declines are recorded and clients are referred without a diagnosis

knowledgeChecks.question: A client has a red, swollen nail bed and asks for gel polish. What is the correct action?
options: Apply gel polish with a barrier layer
Decline the service, record it and suggest a health professional
Apply gel polish only to the unaffected nails

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a technician check the council position before offering artificial nails?
options: Councils set the price of each service
Some councils classify artificial nail work as higher-risk and require registration
Councils only regulate nail salons, not mobile work

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a technician say when declining a service for a suspected infection?
options: What was observed, and a suggestion to see a health professional
Nothing, to avoid upsetting the client
